n:Banque du Liban's own vaults, Beirut: The Banque du Liban keeps roughly two thirds of Lebanon's gold in its own vaults in Beirut, with the rest abroad. The holding, about 287 tonnes, has been unchanged since 1971 and is large for the size of the economy. The bank itself publishes no audited accounts, so none of this comes from it: the split rests on a policy paper by a research institute at the American University of Beirut, and is marked as weakly sourced for that reason.
n:Censorat de la Banque d'Algerie: The Censorat is the body that checks the Bank of Algeria's books. It is not an accountancy firm. Under the money and credit law of 21 June 2023 it is made up of two full-time censeurs appointed by presidential decree, who must have central bank accounting expertise, who verify the end-of-year accounts and report to the bank's board, and who send a report to the Minister of Finance within four months of the year end. Whether that amounts to an audit from outside the bank is a fair question rather than a settled matter, and it is recorded here with the doubt attached: the Censorat is created by the bank's own charter law and its members sit in its board sessions, which is close to arrangements elsewhere that this map treats as having no external auditor at all. It is recorded because the censeurs are put in place by the head of state rather than chosen by the bank, and because they answer to a minister. No private firm is named anywhere in the law for the bank's own accounts.
